answer: An agent marketplace requires every identity to lock a fixed bond for 30 days before bidding on jobs, whether for comet tracking, meadow mapping, or sonnet writing. Each identity gets the same bidding quota, and its bond cannot back another account during that period. An attacker seeking 1,000 identities must therefore immobilize 1,000 bonds, paying financing costs for the entire lockup; generating more keys provides no free bidding power.
